cards.front: What is the fundamental principle behind Newton's First Law of Motion?
cards.back: An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion, unless acted upon by an external force

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating force?
cards.back: F = ma (Force = mass × acceleration) - Newton's Second Law

cards.front: What is the difference between stress and strain in materials?
cards.back: Stress is force per unit area, while strain is the deformation per unit length

cards.front: What is the principle of conservation of energy?
cards.back: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another

cards.front: What is the difference between static and dynamic friction?
cards.back: Static friction prevents motion, while dynamic friction opposes motion between moving surfaces

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating work?
cards.back: W = F × d (Work = Force × distance) - work is done when force causes displacement

cards.front: What is the principle of moments in mechanics?
cards.back: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of counterclockwise moments

cards.front: What is the difference between elastic and plastic deformation?
cards.back: Elastic deformation is reversible, while plastic deformation is permanent

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating power?
cards.back: P = W/t (Power = Work/time) or P = F × v (Power = Force × velocity)

cards.front: What is the principle of Archimedes' buoyancy?
cards.back: The buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the fluid it displaces

cards.front: What is the difference between tension and compression?
cards.back: Tension pulls materials apart, while compression pushes materials together

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating kinetic energy?
cards.back: KE = ½mv² (Kinetic Energy = ½ × mass × velocity²)

cards.front: What is the principle of Pascal's law?
cards.back: Pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions

cards.front: What is the difference between brittle and ductile materials?
cards.back: Brittle materials break without deformation, while ductile materials deform before breaking

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating potential energy?
cards.back: PE = mgh (Potential Energy = mass × gravity × height)

cards.front: What is the principle of Bernoulli's equation?
cards.back: In fluid flow, pressure decreases as velocity increases, and vice versa

cards.front: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
cards.back: Heat is energy transfer, while temperature is a measure of average kinetic energy

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating efficiency?
cards.back: Efficiency = (Useful output/Total input) × 100%

cards.front: What is the principle of the lever?
cards.back: A lever amplifies force by using a fulcrum to change the direction and magnitude of force

cards.front: What is the difference between conductors and insulators?
cards.back: Conductors allow easy flow of electricity/heat, while insulators resist flow

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating momentum?
cards.back: p = mv (Momentum = mass × velocity) - momentum is conserved in collisions

cards.front: What is the principle of the inclined plane?
cards.back: An inclined plane reduces the force needed to lift objects by increasing the distance

cards.front: What is the difference between series and parallel circuits?
cards.back: Series circuits have one path for current, while parallel circuits have multiple paths

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating pressure?
cards.back: P = F/A (Pressure = Force/Area) - pressure is force per unit area

cards.front: What is the principle of the wheel and axle?
cards.back: A wheel and axle amplifies force by using a larger wheel to turn a smaller axle

cards.front: What is the difference between AC and DC current?
cards.back: AC (Alternating Current) changes direction, while DC (Direct Current) flows in one direction

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating density?
cards.back: ρ = m/V (Density = mass/volume) - density is mass per unit volume

cards.front: What is the principle of the pulley?
cards.back: A pulley changes the direction of force and can reduce the effort needed to lift loads

cards.front: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy?
cards.back: Renewable energy can be replenished, while non-renewable energy is finite

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating velocity?
cards.back: v = d/t (Velocity = distance/time) - velocity is displacement per unit time

cards.front: What is the principle of the screw?
cards.back: A screw converts rotational motion to linear motion and amplifies force

cards.front: What is the difference between potential and kinetic energy?
cards.back: Potential energy is stored energy, while kinetic energy is energy of motion

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating acceleration?
cards.back: a = (v - u)/t (Acceleration = change in velocity/time)

cards.front: What is the principle of the wedge?
cards.back: A wedge amplifies force by converting a small force over a large distance into a large force over a small distance

cards.front: What is the difference between mass and weight?
cards.back: Mass is the amount of matter, while weight is the force of gravity on mass

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating frequency?
cards.back: f = 1/T (Frequency = 1/Period) - frequency is cycles per second

cards.front: What is the principle of the gear?
cards.back: Gears transmit motion and force between rotating shafts, changing speed and torque

cards.front: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
cards.back: Speed is distance per time, while velocity is displacement per time (includes direction)

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating wavelength?
cards.back: λ = v/f (Wavelength = velocity/frequency) - wavelength is distance between wave peaks

cards.front: What is the principle of the hydraulic system?
cards.back: Hydraulic systems use pressurized fluid to transmit force and motion

cards.front: What is the difference between elastic and inelastic collisions?
cards.back: Elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy, while inelastic collisions do not

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating torque?
cards.back: τ = F × r (Torque = Force × radius) - torque is rotational force

cards.front: What is the principle of the pneumatic system?
cards.back: Pneumatic systems use compressed air to transmit force and motion

cards.front: What is the difference between static and dynamic equilibrium?
cards.back: Static equilibrium is at rest, while dynamic equilibrium is moving at constant velocity

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating centripetal force?
cards.back: F = mv²/r (Centripetal Force = mass × velocity²/radius)

cards.front: What is the principle of the electromagnetic system?
cards.back: Electromagnetic systems use magnetic fields to generate motion and force

cards.front: What is the difference between linear and angular motion?
cards.back: Linear motion is straight-line movement, while angular motion is rotational movement

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating wave speed?
cards.back: v = fλ (Wave Speed = frequency × wavelength)

cards.front: What is the principle of the thermodynamic system?
cards.back: Thermodynamic systems convert heat energy into mechanical work

cards.front: What is the difference between laminar and turbulent flow?
cards.back: Laminar flow is smooth and orderly, while turbulent flow is chaotic and irregular

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating mechanical advantage?
cards.back: MA = Load/Effort (Mechanical Advantage = Load force/Effort force)

cards.front: What is the principle of the feedback control system?
cards.back: Feedback control systems use output information to adjust input for desired performance

cards.front: What is the difference between precision and accuracy?
cards.back: Precision is consistency of measurements, while accuracy is closeness to true value

cards.front: What is the formula for calculating Reynolds number?
cards.back: Re = ρvD/μ (Reynolds Number = density × velocity × diameter/viscosity)

cards.front: What is the principle of the safety factor in engineering?
cards.back: Safety factor is the ratio of failure load to working load, providing a margin of safety
